newsitem.title: UK: China seen planning international bond -bankers.
newsitem.headline: China seen planning international bond -bankers.

text.p: China plans to raise money in the international capital market but any further details are vague, bankers said on Tuesday.
"Yes, China is definitely eyeing the market and I don't think it is too far away from deciding what to do," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.

A syndicate official at a German bank in Frankfurt said: "China is looking around in the market, however what currency they are eyeing is vague. We hope for more clues in the near future as it is still a bit unclear."
China was reported to be eyeing the mark sector and CSFB and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell were tipped as joint lead managers for the transaction.
In June last year China launched a $700 million five-year global bond via joint lead managers CSFB and Morgan Stanley.
The bond was priced to yield 80 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, last trading around 52 b.p. dealers said.
This deal was quickly followed by a $300 million 10-year bond via the same lead managers. It was priced to yield 110 b.p. over, last trading around 80 b.p. over.
China is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB by Standard & Poor's Corp.
Meanwhile several Chinese institutions earlier this year announced their intentions to tap the international bond market in 1997.
